text:
maria: Heads-up — audit ingestion cost spiked in us-east-1 over the last 2h (~3.4x). Some customers flagged missing 'role_change' events. @leo can you sanity-check ingest logs?
ajay: Yep, saw the alert. ES indexing IOPS are up; lots of events are hitting dynamic mapping for `details` blob -> mapped as text/keyword, causing heavy merges.
leo: Replaying samples -> many events include full request/response bodies. Customers are enabling `include_payload: true`. That explains size + KMS envelope CPU pressure.
sara: Which KMS path are we using? Per-tenant CMK or a shared RW key?
maria: Per-tenant CMK for enterprise customers, default tenant key for self-serve. KMS calls + envelope crypto add ~30-60ms/event when payload > ~1.5KB.
ingest-bot: Dropped 1.2k events in last 10m due to queue overflow at shard-12.
ajay: Oof. So pressure points are payload size, KMS latency, and ES mapping churn.
leo: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) strip payload before indexing and store encrypted blob in cold S3 (index only metadata) 2) batch KMS envelope ops + local envelope cache for active tenants 3) tighten mapping to stop mapping `details` as text 4) per-tenant write QoS/ingest windows 5) configurable per-customer sampling for payloads.
sara: +1 to S3 cold-store for full payloads. That reduces ES costs. We need a fast replay path (S3 + manifest) for compliance customers.
maria: For customer-facing validation we should ship a contract: canonical schema with fields (tenant_id, actor, action, timestamp, resource_id, event_hash, payload_ref) and a lightweight validation webhook that can reject malformed events at the edge.
leo: Minimal suggested schema snippet:
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "rfc3339",
  "actor": "string",
  "action": "string",
  "resource_id": "string",
  "event_hash": "sha256",
  "payload_ref": "s3://bucket/key.encrypted",
  "payload_size": "int"
}
```
ajay: If we add `event_hash` we can do idempotency/dedupe at ingest without decrypting everything. Cheap dedupe before KMS decrypt.
sara: Envelope caching reduces KMS calls but is a policy problem for tenants requiring per-event HSM operations. Need per-tenant policy flags.
maria: Agreed. For tenants that require per-event HSM ops route to dedicated ingest pool with stricter SLOs. Default path: cold-store + metadata.
leo: Also consider a small batching window (e.g., 50ms) to group small events into a single KMS envelope operation — reduces KMS ops but increases tail latency a bit.
ajay: Quick cost note: avg event ~1.2KB, 10M/day => ~12GB/day raw. Indexing full bodies multiplies ES storage and IO; moving bodies to S3 could cut ES storage ~90% and indexing CPU ~60% (rough). KMS ops at 10M/day are expensive; batching could cut ops 6-10x.
sara: We also need a support runbook and customer FAQ: how sampling/redaction affects compliance/auditability and how to request full replay.
maria: I'll draft the customer FAQ + schema contract. Action items: @leo - fix shard hotspot mapping + create index template; @ajay - prototype envelope-batching/cache with tenant TTL; @sara - draft customer-facing validation contract + support runbook. I'll open tickets.
leo: On it. Starting with mapping template to avoid dynamic text mapping and reindex plan.
ingest-bot: ticket #IN-4821 created by maria: audit-ingest: mapping-fix + cold-store plan.
maria: Thanks all. Ping me if you need emergency rollback. :thumbsup:
